posts.caption:
We almost shipped an AI agent that emailed the wrong client. Here's the rule that saved us. 🛑

The agent was fast. Too fast. It drafted, it sent, it moved on — and one wrong draft would've gone straight to a customer.

So we added one line to the system:

"Draft only. Require human approval before anything leaves the building."

That single guardrail changed everything:
• Speed of AI ✅
• Judgment of a human ✅
• Zero "oh no" moments ✅

Autonomy isn't about removing humans. It's about removing the busywork *and keeping the human on the trigger.*

Where would you draw the approval line in your workflow?

posts.caption:
By 2027, "headcount" won't only mean humans. Here's why that's good news. 🤖

For decades, scaling a team meant hiring, onboarding, and hoping. Slow. Expensive. Risky.

Now there's a second option: digital employees that handle the repeatable work — inbox triage, reporting, scheduling, content — and hand the judgment calls back to you.

The winners won't be the companies with the most people. They'll be the ones who pair a small, sharp human team with a fleet of AI teammates doing the busywork.

This isn't humans *vs* AI. It's humans *plus* AI — and the gap between the two camps is about to get very wide.

If you could add one digital teammate to your team tomorrow, what would it do all day?
